Each node is shaded by its authority score. D is pointed to by all three hubs and scores 0.82, B and C 0.41, while the source A and E, fed only by D, score 0." width="100%"} HITS (Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search) computes authority and hub scores for nodes in a directed graph. Authority score measures how much a node is pointed to by good hubs: `authority(v) = sum of hub scores of nodes pointing to v` and, in turn, a node is a good hub if it points to good authorities (see `hub_centrality()`). The two scores are defined in terms of each other, so they are computed together by power iteration: starting from all-ones vectors, each round recomputes authorities from the current hub scores and hubs from the current authority scores, then rescales both vectors to unit Euclidean length. The process stops when neither vector changes by more than `tol=` between rounds, or after `max_iter=` rounds. Authority scores are a natural fit for networks where an edge is an endorsement: - citation networks (papers cited by influential review papers) - the web (pages linked to by good directories or link lists) - recommendation or follower graphs (accounts followed by well-connected curators) Unlike in-degree, which counts every incoming edge equally, authority rewards being pointed to by nodes that themselves point to many good targets. With `weighted=`, each edge passes on its weight times the hub score of its source, so heavier links count for more. Parallel edges add up, so two `A -> B` edges count like one edge of twice the weight, which is also what NetworkX's `hits()` does with a multigraph. The graph must be directed. Each iteration takes time proportional to the number of edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of power-iteration rounds. Defaults to `100`. If the scores have not converged by then, the values from the last round are returned without a warning, so increase this for large graphs or when `tol=` is very small. Very small values (such as `1` or `2`) give rough approximations dominated by in-degree. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold. Iteration stops once the sum of absolute changes between two consecutive rounds is below `tol=` for both the authority and the hub vector. Defaults to `1e-6`. Larger values stop earlier with less precise scores. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, each edge counts with its weight (`1` where missing), and weights must not be negative. If `False`, every edge counts `1`. If `None` (default), follows whether the graph was created as weighted. NetworkX's `hits()` always reads the `"weight"` attribute, so pass `weighted=True` to match it. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name used to store the scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), the column is named `"authority_centrality"`. An existing column with the same name is overwritten. Only used when `return_dict=` is `False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the scores as a dictionary and leave the node DataFrame untouched. If `False` (default), store the scores under `attr_name=` and return the graph for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to authority scores. The scores are non-negative and normalized so that their squares sum to `1`. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is undirected, or if `weighted=` is in effect and an edge has a negative weight. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this small citation network, "Paper1" cites both "Paper2" and "Paper3". The two cited papers share the authority equally, while "Paper1" itself, which nothing cites, scores `0`: ::: {#c1c07a85 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Paper1", "Paper2", "Paper3"]) .add_edges( [ ("Paper1", "Paper2"), # Paper1 cites Paper2 ("Paper1", "Paper3"), # Paper1 cites Paper3 ] ) ) scores = graph.authority_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'Paper1': 0.0, 'Paper3': 0.707, 'Paper2': 0.707} ``` ::: ::: In a slightly larger graph, A points to B, C, and D; B and C also point to D; and D points to E. D is endorsed by all three hubs and gets the top score. E has an incoming edge too, but only from D, which is a poor hub, so its authority converges to `0`: ::: {#5e21bb11 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) scores = graph.authority_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'A': 0.0, 'B': 0.408, 'C': 0.408, 'D': 0.816, 'E': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: Capping the iterations with `max_iter=` shows the scores before convergence: after two rounds E still has a noticeable authority score, because the early hub scores are essentially out-degrees and D does have an outgoing edge: ::: {#b95edb40 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} rough = graph.authority_centrality(max_iter=2, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(rough.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'A': 0.0, 'B': 0.452, 'C': 0.452, 'D': 0.754, 'E': 0.151} ``` ::: ::: With `return_dict=False` (the default) the scores are stored in the node DataFrame and the graph is returned, ready for further chaining: ::: {#24d09453 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .authority_centrality(attr_name="authority") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "authority"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
